author: Wesley Kambale, Roland Sankara
title: Pearl-Chat: Engineering a native Luganda language model from first principles in JAX and Flax NNX
content:
arXiv:2610.22529v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoregressive foundation language models predominantly target high-resource Indo-European languages, imposing computational and morphological penalties on under-represented African languages. Generic multilingual tokenizers routinely exceed fertility rates of 3.2 tokens per word on agglutinative Bantu languages, degrading context efficiency and inflating latency. We present Pearl-Chat, an 8,473,122-parameter ($\sim$8.5M) causal decoder-only transformer engineered for Luganda (Oluganda, ISO 639-2: lg), a low-resource Niger-Congo Bantu language spoken by over 10 million people in East Africa. Built from first mathematical principles in JAX and Flax NNX, Pearl-Chat uses explicit functional state decomposition (nnx.split and nnx.merge), deterministic resumable data streaming via Google Grain, and SPMD tensor parallelism using jax.sharding.Mesh. We introduce a byte-level byte-pair encoding (BPE) subword tokenizer trained from scratch on curated Luganda corpora ($V = 8,192$), achieving 4.88 characters per token compression and 1.60 tokens per word fertility, a two-fold compression improvement over LLaMA-3 (128K) and Gemma (256K). The model is trained with a two-stage curriculum: Stage 1 pre-training on 59,501 sequences across parallel, biblical, encyclopedic, and journalistic corpora, and Stage 2 instruction fine-tuning on 510 dialogues with assistant-only loss masking. Across 4,000 optimization steps, validation cross-entropy loss drops monotonically from 9.4695 (perplexity: 12,958.98) to 0.1818 (perplexity: 1.20), a decrease of 9.2877 nats. On a three-tier held-out diagnostic benchmark, Pearl-Chat achieves 0.9792 ROUGE-L and 0.9405 BLEU while maintaining concordial agreement across Bantu noun classes. We provide a Python Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming runtime and open-source all weights, tokenizers, and code.

author: Adib Sakhawat, Syed Rifat Raiyan
title: Literal Lock-In: How Test Language Shifts Literal Attraction in Typed Decision Models on Bengali Idioms
content:
arXiv:2610.22526v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Decision models, non-generative scorers that report a probability over caller-supplied options and emit no text, are increasingly deployed as routers, classifiers and guardrails. Because they generate nothing, rationales and chain-of-thought do not apply. We audit three: an encoder scorer, a decoder scorer and a closed API, entirely through interventions on their input, using expert-annotated Bengali idioms carrying a gold figurative and a gold literal gloss. Dropping an idiom's own literal gloss into the option list draws every arm toward it, taking 65% to 96% of each arm's remaining Bengali errors. A model-by-language matrix over one shared item set shows how far this depends on the test language: every arm is 1.9 to 6.4 times more captured in Bengali than in English on the same paired entries, the commercial model's apparent resistance is a property of its test language, and capability does not order the failure. Calibration degrades in all three arms, and on the open arms confidence inverts, so gating on it is worse than gating at random. On a semantics-free option list, where accuracy is at chance, the best-calibrated arm still reports mean confidence 0.82. Code and data: https://github.com/sakhadib/literal-lock-in.

author: Hasan Alkhder, Maher Pasa, Maria Hanini, Amro Najjar, Ahmet Zengin
title: alkhder at AlexandriaX-2026: Context-Aware English-to-Dialectal Arabic Dialogue Translation with QLoRA-Fine-Tuned NileChat-3B
content:
arXiv:2610.22525v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper describes team Alkhder's submission to Subtask 1 of the AlexandriaX-2026 shared task, which asks systems to translate English dialogue turns into thirteen Arabic dialects. We fine-tune NileChat-3B-Base with QLoRA on the Alexandria parallel dialogue corpus, training one set of adapter weights for all dialects. Each turn is translated conditioned on the target country and dialect, the domain, the participant roles, the speaker-addressee gender direction, and the preceding dialogue context. At inference, conversations are translated autoregressively and the model is fed its own previous outputs back as context without using any gold target-side test information. Under the constrained track, using only Alexandria data, it trains in about one hour and translates the private test set in under two hours. The system reaches a country-macro-averaged spBLEU of 20.36 and chrF++ of 36.64 on both tracks.

author: Shuhaib Mehri, Philippe Laban, Michel Galley, Dilek T\"ur, Jennifer Neville, Jianfeng Gao
title: Learning User Representations to Improve Simulation Fidelity
content:
arXiv:2610.22518v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: User simulators enable interactive training and evaluation of AI assistants at scale. Yet current simulators struggle to reproduce the diverse behaviors of real users, leading to assistants that generalize poorly to underrepresented users. We identify user representations as an underexplored bottleneck in user simulation. User representations are natural-language descriptions that condition simulators to reproduce a particular user's behavior. A representation's quality becomes apparent in hindsight, through the behavior it induces in a simulator. To evaluate and optimize user representations, we formulate a conversation reconstruction task: given an original conversation, we generate a representation, condition a simulator on it, simulate a conversation, and then measure fidelity by comparing user behavior in the original and simulated conversations. This comparison also yields hindsight feedback, which identifies where the representation falls short and how it can be improved. We introduce hindsight distillation, an online training procedure that distills feedback-conditioned improvements into the representation generator, enabling it to generate improved representations directly from the original conversation. We present UserRepGen-4B, a representation generator trained with hindsight distillation. Across 700 conversations spanning seven datasets, hindsight feedback helps improve user representations at test time, and UserRepGen-4B generates representations that enable more faithful simulation than those generated by GPT-5.5. Beyond conversation reconstruction, learned representations improve simulation fidelity for unseen tasks, better preserve the population-level diversity of real users, and better distinguish users across conversations.

author: Maher Pasa, Maria Hanini, Amro Najjar, Hasan Alkhder
title: alkhder at ImageEval 2026 Shared Tasks: Constrained Selection and Rotation-Averaged Logit Scoring for Multimodal Hallucination Detection
content:
arXiv:2610.22515v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We describe our submission to Subtask~1b of ImageEval 2026. The task consists of selecting the single visually valid statement from three candidates paired with an image, and is in both English and Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). Our system uses a pre-trained 7B vision--language model in a zero-shot setting, without task-specific training or fine-tuning. We formulate the task as a constrained selection problem and choose the answer using next-token log-probabilities. To reduce answer-position bias, we apply a Latin-square rotation to the candidate statements. Our system achieves CI scores of 0.0510 on the English test set and 0.0960 on the MSA test set, reducing CI relative to the official 3B baselines reported on devtest by 83.7\% and 80.4\%, respectively.

author: Shreeyans Arora, Utsav Avaiya, Zera Lyngkhoi, Hem Gosalia, Ram Mohan Rao Kadiyala, Vinay Kumar Sanka
title: AuditKIT: A Unified Evaluation Spine for Benchmarking, Judging, and Comparing Large Language Models and Agentic Systems
content:
arXiv:2610.22511v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluating language models and agents requires combining benchmark accuracy, judge-based assessment, runtime performance, tool-use behavior, and retrieval quality. Differences in interfaces, metric semantics, and trace formats complicate these comparisons and can hide failures in agentic workflows. We present AuditKIT, a source-available evaluation library that records these measurements in one result representation, with direction-aware metric contracts, configuration fingerprints, and extensible metrics and backends. For agents, it provides turn-aware tool-call matching, separates parallel from sequential execution, and distinguishes verified task outcomes from trajectory-level diagnostics. Missing or unobservable evidence is marked unscored rather than counted as failure. For retrieval-augmented generation, it combines ranked retrieval metrics, judged grounding, and deterministic evidence checks. Seven case studies spanning model comparison, serving runtimes, retrieval, tool calling, and interoperability show how answer extraction, runtime behavior, and metric selection change evaluation outcomes.

author: Yunqi Liu, Peiyu Wang, Bingli Wang, Leo Luo, Xuanwu Song, Xudong Ma, Hongxin Li, Yaxin Du, Weicheng
title: RealCLI: Toward a Unified Evaluation of Human-Agent Collaboration for CLI Agents
content:
arXiv:2610.22507v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Command-line interface (CLI) agents increasingly execute longer-horizon tasks, yet existing benchmarks either assume that user instructions remain fixed throughout execution or evaluate task outcomes without capturing runtime collaboration quality. In this paper, we present REALCLI, a paired benchmark that unifies the evaluation of task execution and human-agent collaboration quality on realistic CLI tasks. To comprehensively measure collaboration, REALCLI builds a five-dimensional framework, operationalized into 22 sub-dimensions and 51 interaction scenario templates. REALCLI provides two modes for paired comparison: REALCLI-EXEC supplies complete specifications upfront, whereas REALCLI-COLLAB introduces a scripted user that delivers progressive information, corrections, constraint revisions, and authorization decisions. Evaluations reveal profound capability gaps in frontier agents: the best configuration attains an average score of only 49.2%, and when evaluated by the joint collaboration score ($J_{\mathrm{collab}}$), the peak performance reaches merely 37.6%. These results show that task effectiveness diverges sharply from collaboration quality, with models consistently struggling in steerability, trust calibration, and safety boundary management. REALCLI provides a rigorous, reproducible foundation for measuring and advancing collaborative CLI agents.

author: Iskar Deng, Shane Steinert-Threlkeld
title: From Parallels to Divergence: Language Models' Learning of Action Nominal Constructions
content:
arXiv:2610.22468v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Action nominal constructions (ANCs) express events in nominal form, with their argument marking following patterns found in clauses or ordinary noun phrases. In this paper, we investigate how different grammatical configurations affect language models' learning of ANCs and related constructions, and how these learning preferences compare with typological distributions in natural languages. We use a grammar-engineered method for synthetic corpus construction that combines shared semantic input from natural corpora with computational grammars. We construct 96 target languages varying in clause word order, noun-phrase word order, alignment, complement system, and ANC strategy. For each language, we train GPT-2-small models from scratch and evaluate them using targeted minimal pairs covering 34 grammatical phenomena. The results show typological parallels in basic clause configurations but divergences in complement systems and ANC strategies, with models also learning combinations rare or unattested in natural languages. This partial alignment suggests that natural language distributions may reflect both general learning pressures and functional demands not fully captured by model learning experiments.

author: Zhiyuan Wang
title: Where Prefill Expert Reduction Hurts MoE Models: A Few Prompt Tokens Carry Most of the Short-Answer F1 Loss
content:
arXiv:2610.22454v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Running prompt tokens through fewer routed experts during prefill is a simple way to make mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving cheaper, yet it is unclear what this damages. We locate the damage with token-, layer- and attention-path interventions on short-answer question answering in four MoE families. At half the experts the F1 loss of three families is mostly answer form: the model still finds the answer but stops answering briefly. In Qwen3-30B-A3B this loss is made at the two chat-template tokens before the answer, and in DeepSeek-V2-Lite at the first 8-32 prompt tokens, where its instruction sits; by answer likelihood these positions account for about half and a fifth of the damage. Reduction changes the first token's attention mass, norm and largest activation by less than 4%, and restoring super experts or massive activations recovers at most about a quarter of the loss, well below keeping the sensitive positions full. On real prompts with about 4% of tokens at full experts, placing them on the task interface keeps F1 within one point of the unmodified model, while placing them at random in the documents is about 3 points worse (two of five prespecified primary comparisons; the others were undecided or not run). Because the answer boundary always ends a single-turn prompt, and DeepSeek's loss was no longer detectable once its instruction moved away from the start, the sensitive tokens lay at the prompt ends in every sensitive layout we found, so rules that keep the ends are not distinguished from rules that read application marks. Time to first token falls about 14% on 11K-token prompts and not at 2K tokens.

author: Sai Kiran Bathula
title: Embeddings Are Overpriced? A Frozen 16 MB Vocabulary for Small and Ternary Language Models
content:
arXiv:2610.22428v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In a small language model the vocabulary is the single largest part. In Gemma 3 270M the embedding table holds 168M of 268M parameters, and because quantisation methods leave the embedding in 16-bit, it is also most of the file once the rest of the model is compressed. We ask what that table actually buys. We replace it with one frozen table of 512-bit codes, 16 MB, with no trainable parameters, derived once from a pretrained embedding by principal-component projection and sign binarisation, and we train the same Gemma-shaped body from scratch on the same 2.05B tokens with and without it. The learned table buys 0.20 nats of validation loss for 2.6 times the trainable parameters, but on LAMBADA, HellaSwag and PIQA the frozen-table model is better or tied; only ARC-Easy favours the learned table. With a ternary BitNet b1.58 body the whole model is a 46 MB file, still ties the float model on LAMBADA and PIQA, and on a laptop CPU generates 615 to 740 tokens per second in 62 MB of memory, five to six times the speed of the float model's 8-bit GGUF in llama.cpp at a seventh of the memory. The frozen table wins by 1.7 to 2.3 nats on rare words, accepts 10,000 new words after training with a 3% cost where the learned table collapses by 43%, and all of it is released with the weights, the data and every evaluation answer.

author: Alloy Das, Shreyan Ganguly, Nyzil Massey, Hung Phi Doan, Zhanhong Jiang, Thimmasettappa Thippeswamy,
title: Seeing Seizures: A Large-Scale Empirical Study of Video and EEG Deep Learning for Automated Rodent Seizure Detection and Severity Grading
content:
arXiv:2610.22566v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Manual annotation of synchronized video and EEG recordings is a bottleneck in preclinical seizure research. We present an empirical study of seizure detection and behavioral severity grading using 24,131 paired clips from 601 sessions across 20 rats in a soman-induced epilepsy model. Ten video architectures and seven single-channel EEG models are evaluated independently on binary detection and three- and five-class severity tasks. In the session-exclusive reference comparison, R(2+1)D-18 and GRU achieve detection macro-F1 scores of 0.968 and 0.974, respectively; for five-class grading, the corresponding scores are 0.657 and 0.560. Subject-exclusive evaluation reduces five-class macro-F1 to 0.475 for video and 0.404 for EEG, highlighting the difficulty of grading unseen animals. Temporal-sampling experiments demonstrate the value of multiple frames, while detection performance varies relatively little across the evaluated video architectures. A separate video-only binary-detection evaluation on RodEpil achieves a mean seizure-class F1 of 0.979 after uniform re-encoding to reduce identified class-correlated encoding cues. The study characterizes existing models for behavior-defined severity labels under the evaluated protocol, motivating further investigation of expert-assisted annotation workflows. Our code and github page is available here.

author: Madison Van Horn, Suzanne Stathatos, Sevan Brodjian, Justin Kay, Kai Van Brunt, Erik Young, Sara Bee
title: CFC26: Building Evaluations for Deployment in Sonar-Based Fish Counting
content:
arXiv:2610.22549v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate counts of fish populations are essential for monitoring ecosystems and making decisions for conservation, harvest limits, and river management. In many field deployments, these counts are obtained from sonar videos that experts must inspect manually, making large-scale monitoring slow, expensive, and difficult. Automated counting systems have been proposed as a scalable alternative, but so far this promise has been difficult to realize in deployment. Developing evaluations that better reflect real-world deployment conditions will help close this gap and drive improvements in counting performance in practice. To achieve this, we propose Caltech Fish Counting 2026 (CFC26), a new dataset with improved evaluation protocols that simulate deployment to seen and novel rivers, testing in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance. We expand the CFC22 dataset to eleven deployment locations across nine Pacific salmon river systems from Alaska to Northern California, capturing a broader geographical and ecological range of data. We additionally introduce two new evaluation metrics for counting, nMNE and nMANE, that mirror the operational workflow that experts use and help surface errors that frame-level detection metrics do not capture. Using these metrics, we reveal previously-concealed directional bias in upstream vs downstream counts, which would have direct and significant ecological implications if undetected. The dataset and code are publicly available on CaltechDATA and GitHub.

author: Ngan Nguyen, Dung Nguyen, Quan Dao, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Minh Hoai, Cuong Pham, Anh Tran
title: FlashControl: One-Step Controllable Generator via Distillation-Friendly Single-Stream Teachers
content:
arXiv:2610.22537v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion models have become a leading approach in visual generative modeling, particularly effective in text-to-image and controllable generation. Their main drawback is slow inference as it requires many sampling steps. While recent distillation methods enable one-step text-to-image generation, extending these techniques to controllable generation is still challenging. Existing controllable models, such as ControlNet, rely on dual-branch design that make distillation difficult. In this work, we adopt a simpler strategy. Instead of adding extra conditional branches, we finetune a selected subset of layers in the original text-to-image diffusion model to directly enable controllable generation. This results in DeltaControl, a single-flow, multi-step diffusion model capable of supporting spatial-condition generation while matching the performance of dual-branch approaches. Building on this teacher model, we further apply step-distillation to obtain FlashControl, a one-step model capable of spatial controllable generation with a single forward pass.

author: Nithin Chalapathi, Theo Sternlieb, Ethan Han, Sonya M. Hanson, Pilar Cossio, Aditi S. Krishnapriyan,
title: Learning the Shared Latent Structure of Cryo-EM Inverse Problems
content:
arXiv:2610.22523v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Understanding biomolecular function requires characterizing three-dimensional structure and conformational variability, for which cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is a powerful tool. Cryo-EM produces noisy two-dimensional particle images in which molecular structure, particle pose, and imaging conditions are jointly encoded. Recovering biological information from these observations spans inverse problems including pose estimation, heterogeneity analysis, and reconstruction. These tasks are usually addressed independently despite shared protein structure and image formation, motivating a common representation across inverse problems. Since biologically meaningful differences may be spatially localized, we study self-distillation with complementary global and masked patch objectives. Because experimental dataset discrimination can reflect acquisition-specific cues, we develop controlled synthetic and experimental evaluations and find that structural discrimination benefits from dense spatial features. We introduce the EMber family of vision transformers, pre-trained on >50 million experimental particle images from 214 EMPIAR datasets together with simulated projections from 268,000 molecular assemblies. EMber improves upon existing methods at conformational and compositional discrimination by 14.85 and 14.26 percentage points, estimates conformational populations to within 1.59pp error with a linear probe, and produces particle assignments yielding reference-quality reconstructions in fewer epochs. We demonstrate how to learn representations that capture biological information for use across multiple cryo-EM inverse problems.

author: Nicky Kriplani, Yiwen Zhang, Angelina Wang, Hadar Averbuch-Elor
title: Towards Reconstructing Geographically Diverse Architecture with 3D Foundation Models
content:
arXiv:2610.22514v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Internet-scale photo collections of real-world landmarks have driven progress in 3D computer vision yet remain highly challenging for modern 3D foundation models (3DFMs) that estimate scene structure in a single feed-forward pass. In this work, we introduce ArchWorld, a benchmark of 3D architectural landmarks with high geographic coverage and rich metadata. We use this benchmark to conduct a thorough error analysis of current 3DFMs to understand where they fall short and how they can be improved. We examine socially relevant disparities in model error and find that model performance varies by geographic region; however, unlike typical fairness regimes, the trends only partially match training data representation. Our investigation reveals that the observed geographic disparities reflect not only differences in data representation and scene size but also differences in region-specific architectural features and background distractors that make scenes from different regions inherently vary in difficulty. Leveraging insights from these model failings, we introduce an intervention scheme that improves 3DFM performance while simultaneously reducing geographic disparities.

author: Markus Kramer, Jan Wachenfeld, Oskar von Stryk
title: TriSAR-3D and PaintFusion: A Novel Trimodal LiDAR-RGB-Thermal Dataset and Method for 3D Person Detection in Search and Rescue
content:
arXiv:2610.22509v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reliable 3D person detection is important for rescue robotics to give first responders situational awareness. Yet most multimodal 3D detection research targets automotive scenarios in which pedestrians mostly appear in a narrow range of upright, near-road poses. It is therefore unclear how much of the reported performance transfers to rescue settings, as a person may be lying, partially occluded, or in unstructured indoor and outdoor environments. To investigate this gap, we introduce TriSAR-3D, a multimodal person detection dataset recorded with a high-resolution 128-channel LiDAR, an RGB camera, and a thermal camera. It captures varied poses in indoor as well as outdoor locations at different times of day to study their influence on 3D object detector performance. Furthermore, we propose a novel trimodal 3D detection pipeline, PaintFusion, that fuses PointPainting-based evidence using a simple MLP. We show that the derived method reaches 65.4 AP@50 and thereby outperforms strong LiDAR-only (CenterPoint, 53.4), RGB+LiDAR (BEVFusion, 60.5), and adapted trimodal (Tri-BEVFusion, 60.7) baselines on the dataset. At the same time, it is substantially faster than other fusion-based methods such as BEVFusion, with a per-frame latency of 51.6 ms compared to 101 ms. Additionally, we test how the performance of different 3D object detectors generalizes to unseen pose categories. Removing lying instances from training data collapses the lying-pose AP@50 to near zero across all evaluated detectors. The results indicate that dataset diversity exerts a large effect on 3D object detection performance. The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/MarkusKramer1/3D-Trimodal-People-Detection.

author: Xinwei Ju, Zhehua Mao, Tianyi Song, Danail Stoyanov, Sophia Bano, Francisco Vasconcelos
title: KFS$^4$LAM: Adaptive KeyFrame Selection with Structure-Aware Mapping for Endoscopic Gaussian Splatting SLAM
content:
arXiv:2610.22505v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gaussian-splatting Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) augments conventional SLAM with a dense, renderable 3D scene representation, enabling high-quality reconstruction and novel-view synthesis. However, its localization, reconstruction, and rendering performance depends strongly on which observations are retained for mapping. Existing systems commonly rely on fixed temporal intervals or simple pose- and overlap-based criteria for keyframe selection. In colonoscopy, non-uniform camera motion, repetitive anatomy, specularities, and visual artifacts can make these criteria unreliable, leading to either redundant keyframes or missed informative viewpoints. We present KFS$^4$LAM (KeyFrame Selection with Structure-aware mapping for endoscopic Gaussian Splatting SLAM), which couples motion-guided adaptive keyframe selection with structurally supervised mapping and restricted temporal deformation. Accumulated motion guides adaptive keyframe selection, with complementary cues suppressing redundant or unreliable candidates. Density-aware mapping with anatomical contour supervision (colon folds) emphasizes structurally informative regions, while restricted temporal deformation accommodates local tissue dynamics without unconstrained geometric drift. We evaluate KFS$^4$LAM against Gaussian-SLAM baselines on C3VD and C3VD-v2, together with cross-backbone and component ablations. KFS$^4$LAM achieves strong overall performance across trajectory, rendering, and depth metrics, with pronounced gains on more challenging C3VD-v2 dataset. In the matched comparison with SplaTAM on C3VD-v2, it reduces rotational relative pose error by 20.3% and depth RMSE by 38.4%, while improving PSNR by 0.78 dB. Cross-backbone experiments further show that the framework is not tied to a single underlying SLAM architecture. Code and visualization results are available at https://xinweiju.github.io/KFSLAM/.

author: Junseok Ahn, Jaehyun Park, Jeongsoo Choi, Joon Son Chung, Ji-Hoon Kim
title: JAVIS: Joint Audio-Visual Interaction and Streaming for Real-Time Conversational Agents
content:
arXiv:2610.22499v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Human communication is inherently multimodal, conveying intent not only through linguistic and vocal cues but also through visual signals. However, existing conversational systems have mainly focused on text or speech, leaving out the visual feedback that is essential for natural interaction. In this paper, we propose JAVIS, an end-to-end streaming framework for real-time audio-visual conversational agents. Our key idea is to let the voice and the face speak from a single representation. On top of a shared LLM, a Joint Refined Head produces a unified audio-visual representation, which is fed into dedicated streaming branches for speech and face generation. This end-to-end design avoids intermediate bottlenecks, enabling real-time generation while keeping speech and face tightly synchronized. In addition, we present JAVIS-Syn, a 334-hour synthetic corpus designed to address the lack of expressive audio-visual dialogue data, covering emotionally rich multi-turn conversations and assistant-style exchanges. Experiments show that JAVIS achieves approximately 200$\times$ lower initial latency than a strong baseline, while outperforming baselines in lip synchronization and facial expression appropriateness.

author: J. P. Naiman
title: Star Light, Star Bright: Can Multimodal Models Parse an Astronomy Visual Question Answering Dataset Right?
content:
arXiv:2610.22474v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Figures are essential for scientific communication, and the field of Visual Question Answering (VQA) aims to test the figure understanding capabilities of large multimodal models (LMMs). Here, we investigate the accuracy of several low-cost LMMs on domain-specific VQA tasks for astronomical images of the sky. As instrument for this task we build a domain-specific VQA dataset comprising 2001 partially-synthetic figures divided evenly between contour plots, real telescope images drawn from NASA's SkyView, and "fake" sky images which share the axes and angular scales of the real images but draw their colors from a gaussian mixture model, alongside 47357 questions. Each figure is released as pristine and with realistic page-aging degradations mimicking the historical astronomical corpus. Testing three low-cost proprietary LMMs, we find models frequently fail to answer domain-specific questions at high accuracy. An initial comparison with 104 human-verified, astrometrically tagged figures from historical journal publications shows similar median errors in angular extent. All code is available on GitHub: https://github.com/jnaiman/SkyImagesWASP2026 and dataset is available on HuggingFace: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ReadingTimeMachine/astro_sky_image_vqa.

author: Yizhe Zhang, Xujia Wang, Songqi Tang, Xujie Tang, Leo Jiahao Jiang, Jiacheng Wang, Bowen Qu, JinBo L
title: Event-STVG: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding for Long-Form Event Reasoning
content:
arXiv:2610.22444v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (STVG) aims to jointly localize a target in space and time given a natural-language query. Despite continued advances, existing STVG benchmarks remain largely centered on localizing targets through instance-specific descriptions, leaving them largely decoupled from long-form reasoning increasingly emphasized in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). In this paper, we introduce Event-STVG, a task that shifts STVG from locating what is described toward event-level reasoning by unifying long-form context, repeated-event reasoning, event localization, role inference, and multi-target grounding. To facilitate research on Event-STVG, we construct a large-scale benchmark comprising 4,016 annotated event occurrences across soccer and seven additional domains. Experiments with state-of-the-art MLLMs reveal substantial difficulty, with the strongest model achieving only 5.4% m-vIoU at the 10-minute horizon. Across domains, we consistently observe confusion among repeated same-type events, spatial grounding bottlenecks, and rare success in jointly grounding all required roles. Event-STVG establishes a new challenge for visual understanding in MLLMs, calling for future models that can jointly reason about complex events across space and time. Code and annotations are available at https://github.com/THU-KEG/EventSTVG

author: Kamil Faber, Katarzyna Filus, {\L}ukasz Pawela
title: Sparse Autoencoders Can Induce Local Geometry for Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting
content:
arXiv:2610.22439v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Catastrophic forgetting remains a challenge in supervised continual learning, as adapting to new tasks causes representation drift and loss of previously learned information. This raises the question of which representational changes should be constrained while preserving plasticity. We therefore introduce Sparse Autoencoder Geometric Anchoring (SAGA), which converts a Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) trained at each task boundary into local, low-rank constraints on representation drift. Replay examples specify where the constraints apply, while leading right singular directions of the encoder Jacobian specify which changes are penalized. The resulting geometry is input dependent and can be retained without keeping the SAE for subsequent tasks' training. We establish its local relation to latent code matching, define its spectral truncation error, and derive a conditional bound on frozen-readout drift. With replay and snapshot history, the method achieves the highest mean Class-IL accuracy and lowest mean forgetting among the evaluated ER, DER++, ER-ACE, and SGD baselines on three pretrained ViT-B/16 benchmarks, with accuracy gains of 12.15, 4.79, and 3.22 percentage points over the strongest conventional baseline on CIFAR-100, CUB-200, and ImageNet-R, respectively. From scratch results are more mixed, while rank ablations and geometry controls show that SAE-induced low-rank geometry offers useful stability-plasticity trade-offs.

author: Muhammad Usman Altaf
title: Rank Measures of Fine-Tuning Updates Need a Noise Baseline
content:
arXiv:2610.22438v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Studies of what fine-tuning does to a language model often summarise the weight update $\Delta W$ by its rank. We compare the rank measures used for this against the same measures on a random matrix of the same shape, and against two harder references: the pretrained weights, and matched fine-tunes without alignment content. Measures that count directions put our fine-tuning updates only a little below noise; stable rank, computed from the same singular values, puts them far below. Both are right: an update has a few strong directions on top of a long tail. The pattern holds for thirteen released pairs up to 8B parameters, and it is not a mark of alignment: with training held fixed, instruction data does not stand out from Wikipedia or code, DPO gives the same update whether its preference labels are real or half swapped at random (one model, modest preference strength), and scrambled text gives the most concentrated update of all. Applied to a recent claim that post-training is superficial because the effective rank of the weights barely changes, the baselines show that a random update of the same size leaves that rank almost unchanged while wrecking the model, and that an edit built on the effective rank of the update has no measurable effect in our tests. Rank measures of weight updates need a noise baseline, and claims about alignment need a control without alignment content.

author: Sabarish G, Deepak Parashar
title: CF-NODE: Counterfactual Spatial Node Intervention for Test-Time Adaptation Under Domain Shift, Evaluated Across Five Diabetic Retinopathy Datasets
content:
arXiv:2610.22437v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated fundus-based diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading can substantially expand screening capacity, but source-trained models degrade sharply across different cameras, clinics, and patient populations. Existing test-time adaptation methods depend on entropy minimization or target information accumulated from image batches and streams. These mechanisms can reinforce confidently incorrect predictions and break down when clinical images arrive independently. We introduce CF-NODE, a novel counterfactual test-time adaptation framework for cross- domain DR grading. Instead of trusting prediction confidence or estimating a target distribution, CF-NODE asks how each prediction responds under a controlled intervention on the evidence supporting it. CF-NODE ranks internal spatial nodes using model-derived attention, feature magnitude, and node-set similarity, progressively attenuates the highest-ranked nodes, and uses the stability of the resulting expected-grade response to apply a bounded calibration of the predicted grade distribution. The framework is fully frozen and adapts every image independently using only geometric views and a fixed source-derived prior, requiring no target-derived information or model updates. We evaluate CF-NODE on five external DR datasets under repeated-seed evaluation against TENT, EATA, SAR, and T3A. CF-NODE outperforms all four methods with statistically significant improvements over the second-best method, improves AUC on every target domain, and attains the highest average AUC and macro-F1, delivering stronger grade discrimination together with more balanced recognition across DR severity levels. These results demonstrate that counterfactual intervention sensitivity provides consistent and deployment-ready domain robustness for single-image clinical inference.

author: Alvaro Peiro, Marios Impraimakis
title: Generative adversarial networks with Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty quantification for structural health monitoring: Fibre Bragg grating data augmentation comparison in Hawk T1A aircraft
content:
arXiv:2610.22436v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The signal generation capabilities of a novel data augmentation framework are examined in aerospace structures. First, the framework learns class-conditional temporal and spectral characteristics of the measured structural responses. It uses conditional generative adversarial network training and Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty quantification as a Bayesian approximation. This step enables stochastic signal synthesis and uncertainty quantification. Second, the generated responses are rigorously compared against experimental measurements across time, frequency, uncertainty, variability, and feature domains to assess physical realism, statistical consistency, and distributional fidelity. Finally, the synthetic data are evaluated to determine whether they should be incorporated into a supervised damage classification workflow. The framework is validated on the full-scale benchmark dataset from a BAE Systems Hawk T1A aircraft tested at the University of Sheffield's Structural Dynamics Laboratory for Verification and Validation. The test involves acceleration, fibre Bragg grating strain, and nonlinear dynamic response measurements. The results demonstrate that the model accurately captures dominant structural dynamics, it guides on signal use for classification improvement based on uncertainty characteristics, and it provides meaningful uncertainty estimates linked to signal complexity and excitation characteristics. Importantly, the framework offers a realistic generative modelling plan as a robust digital twin component for data-driven structural health monitoring, supporting resilient decision-making for condition assessment in safety-critical aerospace systems.

author: Muhammad Azlan Qazi, Alexandros Iosifidis, Qi Zhang
title: TRACE: Transformer Residual Activation Codebook Encoding for Communication-efficient Distributed Edge Inference
content:
arXiv:2610.22435v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distributed Transformer inference across co-located edge devices is fundamentally communication-bound, as exchanging activations between sequence-parallel partitions dominates inference latency under commodity edge bandwidths. Existing compression schemes reduce this cost but retain a structural bottleneck: the received data must still undergo key/value projection before attention can proceed, serializing computation behind communication. This paper presents Transformer Residual Activation Codebook Encoding (Trace), a framework that addresses these limitations. Trace places a Vector Quantizer (VQ) at the post-attention residual of every Transformer layer and precomputes codebook-indexed key/value representations. During inference, exchanged activations are encoded into compact codebook indices, allowing receivers to directly recover keys and values through table lookup instead of executing the downstream computations required to derive them. By eliminating the received data downstream computation, Trace enables communication--computation overlap and reduces a key latency bottleneck in distributed Transformer inference. A hierarchical clustering further structures the learned codebook into a multi-resolution hierarchy, enabling runtime adaptation of the communication bitrate without retraining. The framework supports two operating variants: one prioritizing accuracy and the other balancing accuracy and efficiency through buffer-compatible quantization. Experiments on ViT-Base (ImageNet-1K and CIFAR-100) and ViViT-B (UCF-101) show that Trace achieves up to 1.89% higher accuracy and up to 1.27x end-to-end inference speedup compared with the state-of-the-art VQ-based distributed inference framework. Compared with uncompressed sequence-parallel inference, Trace reduces communication overhead by up to 22,624x.

author: Ziheng Zhang, Wei Zhang, Yunyi Zhao, Zuming Liu, Wei Zhou, Boon Ping Gan
title: BOLT: Multi-Bottleneck Bound-Guided Learning for Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling with Time Lags and Resource-Coupled Transport
content:
arXiv:2610.22433v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Flexible job-shop scheduling becomes resource-coupled when a scarce vehicle fleet moves jobs between stations, because the schedule sets the transport waits. BOLT (bound-oriented learning for transport-coupled scheduling) builds a lower bound from chain, machine-capacity, and fleet-capacity relaxations. The bound equals the makespan at termination, so its per-step changes form a reward that sums to a constant minus the makespan. Because it never exceeds the attainable makespan, each candidate's bound increase is a proven rise of the makespan floor, which the policy reads as a price. The root bound certifies a completed schedule's suboptimality gap without a solver. On industry-motivated 10-module prefabricated-construction instances, explicit transport coupling outperforms a transport-penalty policy in every tested cell where loaded moves occupy at least 66% of fleet time and in none at or below 56%. Across five zero-shot 50- and 80-module production batches, BOLT outperforms the best dispatching-rule pair on four and the penalty policy on the three with long moves. In the three-vehicle 80-module batch, its mean makespan is 13.0% below the best pair and 4.2% below an hour-budget constraint-programming solver whose proven gap averages 34%. BOLT decides in 2.3-5.9 ms per event on one processor core and re-plans a disruption in seconds.

author: Hariharan Srinivasan, Masoom Bhargava, Sayan Gupta
title: CGDT-CESN: Correlation-Guided and Dynamics-Trained Clustered Echo State Network for Multivariate Time-Series Prediction
content:
arXiv:2610.22430v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate prediction of multivariate time series requires models that simultaneously capture variable-specific dynamics and cross-variable interactions. In this work, a Correlation-Guided and Dynamics-Trained Clustered Echo State Network (CGDT-CESN) is proposed, which comprises a modular reservoir architecture with each cluster distinctly specializing in one of the variables in the multivariate time series. An innovative reservoir design is proposed in which inter-cluster connections are enabled by empirically observed correlations among variables, providing a data-driven coupling mechanism. Apart from conventional readout training, inter-cluster connection weights informed by correlations are trained, which in turn allows the reservoir to capture time-varying cross-variable dependencies without sacrificing computational efficiency and further improves forecasting accuracy. The prediction performance of CGDT-CESN is found to be superior to that of the conventional ESN when evaluated on two fundamentally different datasets: Twitter information cascade evolution and solar wind forecasting. Also, the improvement in performance is preserved across multiple prediction horizons, even when presented with a low volume of data. By unifying cluster-specific specialization with learned inter-variable coupling, CGDT-CESN offers a principled, data-driven route to multivariate time series prediction.

author: Zhe Zhou
title: Binding-Specific Relearning Savings for Test-Time Continual Learning
content:
arXiv:2610.22381v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When a fact becomes harder to elicit from a language model, has the model lost it, or has it merely become less accessible? Parameter-updating test-time continual learning agents are usually evaluated by current output accuracy; we ask whether that measurement captures how prior experience shapes later updates. We test whether learning a specific factual binding produces a later relearning advantage beyond familiarity with its entity, answer vocabulary, format, or query slot. In Qwen2.5-1.5B, we compare three matched, counterbalanced histories: LEARNED receives the correct binding, CONTROL receives matched exposure without it, and WRONG receives a competing relation-valid answer in the same slot. After an identical rehearsal-free continual fine-tuning stream, LEARNED reacquires the target faster than CONTROL at a prespecified checkpoint of partial forgetting. WRONG shows no positive advantage over CONTROL, while its comparison with LEARNED provides slot-matched corroboration, subject to possible competitor interference. The advantage remains positive after adjustment for measured pre-relearning behavior. In a secondary descriptive conversion using an unpaired never-seen pool, prior learning reduces the optimizer updates required for restoration by about 18%. Current behavioral accuracy can therefore underestimate the lasting effect of previously acquired experience. Code is available at https://github.com/zhezhou1106/relearning-savings

author: Gunmay Jhingran
title: Trust but Verify: Designing Region-Inhomogeneous Forward Dynamics for Discrete Diffusion
content:
arXiv:2610.22380v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Continuous diffusion treats the forward process as a design space; discrete language diffusion often uses absorbing corruption, leaving context fully trusted throughout generation. This makes trust binary: corrupted context is copied as ground truth, propagating errors into generated spans. We reopen this design space by combining absorbing and uniform-mixing kernels with region-dependent rates. Missing positions follow absorbing dynamics, while context undergoes low-rate random substitution, exposing the model to observed but uncertain tokens during training. At inference, a heuristic sampler re-injects noise into suspicious context under an annealed intensity and freezes context updates late in the trajectory. An 8,000-step finetune of a pretrained 170M-parameter masked diffusion model takes under five hours on a 6 GB laptop GPU. The base model assigns roughly 50% probability to observed tokens even when they are uniform-random garbage. For uniform-random corruption, finetuning detects corrupted context with 0.96 recall and 0.91 precision, improves infill token-F1 by 3.8 points at 10% corruption and 6.4 points at 20%, and removes the accuracy dip next to corruptions. Clean conditioning shows no measurable regression, with a false-edit rate below 0.4%. Gains for plausible corruptions are weaker: about 0.5 F1 points at 10% corruption, without statistical significance. Our results suggest that detectability and damage depend jointly on departure from the data conditional: nearby noise is hard to detect and semantically mild, while distant noise is conspicuous and destructive. We interpret absorbing diffusion as the infinite-contrast limit of a trust axis, analogous to the signal-to-noise gap between known and unknown regions in diffusion inpainting. In our setting of a 170M model and a single text domain, intermediate trust is reached by changing forward dynamics rather than architecture.

author: Ruo-Qian Wang
title: When is a large language model a good calibration agent? Physics-labeled prompting for budgeted engineering simulator calibration
content:
arXiv:2610.22379v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Calibrating expensive engineering simulators requires tuning model parameters to match reference data, a process heavily constrained by computational costs. This study investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs), conditioned on physical diagnostic descriptions of simulation errors, can propose informative parameter updates more efficiently than conventional derivative-free optimizers. We test this on a cylinder-wake Large-Eddy Simulation and a damped-oscillator inverse problem. Physics-labeled prompts are evaluated against four text ablations (removed, anonymized, padded, misdirected) and standard optimizers (Nelder-Mead, Bayesian optimization, CMA-ES, and random search). Results demonstrate a strong early semantic advantage: the first physics-informed LLM proposal improves the initial design in 23 of 25 trials. After five evaluations, the median calibration error is 21.9 times lower than physics-free controls. However, this advantage is transient - disappearing by fifteen evaluations - and inherent LLM decoder variability yields a 9.8-fold performance spread. To address this, we introduce a hybrid workflow that uses the LLM as a warm-start, passing accumulated evaluations to a conventional optimizer. This two-stage numerical continuation policy reaches target accuracy in just 9 simulator runs, outperforming the LLM alone (12 runs), Nelder-Mead (17 runs), and Bayesian optimization (>60 runs). Supported by sensitivity analysis validating the test cases, this hybrid physics-labeled LLM scheme proves highly effective as a calibration agent under strict evaluation budgets.

author: Christian Marowski, Byung-Cheol Min
title: Task Structure and Scalability in Multi-Robot Authoring
content:
arXiv:2610.22670v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-robot authoring can reduce completion time by distributing drawing work, but the resulting speedup depends on task structure and the allocation-routing pipeline. We investigate these relationships by representing drawings as geometric stroke graphs and comparing component-level (single-token) allocation with shared-token (decomposed) allocation, which permits multiple robots to work within a connected component. A simulation study of 385 drawings and teams of one to eight robots shows diminishing speedup gains under single-token allocation and larger mean speedups under the shared-token pipeline, each normalized by its own single-robot completion time. Shared-token execution also exhibits lower idle-time shares at larger team sizes, although it does not reduce completion time for every drawing. Comparisons across structural attribute groups reveal associations between structural descriptors and differences in scaling behavior, with greater separation between several attribute groups at larger team sizes. These findings characterize empirical scaling in the evaluated pipelines and highlight the importance of considering within-component workload and graph structure alongside component count. Additional materials are available at https://sites.google.com/view/multirobotauthoring/home.

author: Narayanan Palghat Parameswaran (Carnegie Mellon University), Dong-Ki Kim (FieldAI), Jay Patrikar (Fi
title: FCTS: Failure-Guided Curriculum Tree Search Over Generated Terrain for Legged Parkour
content:
arXiv:2610.22619v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quadruped parkour policies handle canonical obstacles well, but their training curricula often miss the irregular, compound geometry of industrial and disaster-response sites, where agile locomotion matters most. Such environments pose a hard generalization problem: even training directly on reconstructed geometry from the target site does not reliably yield policies that traverse it. Hand-designed curricula span only a few terrain families, and recent LLM-generated curricula offer little control over which policy weaknesses they target. We propose FCTS, a failure-conditioned terrain curriculum framework that uses localized traversal failures to automatically generate the terrains a policy should train on next. Each failure's location, termination mode, robot state, and surrounding terrain geometry condition this generation, and Monte Carlo Tree Search explores alternative curriculum trajectories under a fixed training budget. On terrains built from scanned real-world construction sites, FCTS raises success rate from 28.4% to 85.8% on a medium-difficulty course and from 14.9% to 44.7% on a hard course relative to the strongest parkour or LLM-curriculum baselines, and maintains higher progress on extreme terrains where full traversal is rare. Hardware experiments on a quadruped robot confirm that the learned FCTS policies transfer to the real world.

author: Devin Han, Hershraj Niranjani
title: Embodiment-Classifier Guidance: Transferring Frozen VLAs Across Robot Dynamics without Demonstrations
content:
arXiv:2610.22576v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Flow-based policies such as $\pi_0$ are trained on a fixed set of embodiments, and transferring them to new ones is an open problem. To adapt a frozen $\pi_0$ to a new embodiment without additional demonstrations or parameter updates, we train a lightweight embodiment classifier to distinguish successful action chunks on the source body from those on the target body, using a few calibration tasks. On transfer tasks that $\pi_0$ saw on its source body but the classifier was never trained on, we nudge each denoising step of $\pi_0$ with the classifier's gradient, which estimates the direction from the distribution of successful actions on the source body toward that on the target body. On the LIBERO simulation benchmark with four modified controllers, embodiment-classifier guidance raises $\pi_0$'s average success on the target bodies from 72% to 80% across 12 suite-controller pairs, with a 31% relative reduction in failures (11 of 12 gain; 5 significant after Holm correction). In simulation, guidance is data-efficient, needing few target-body rollouts per task, which makes it promising for sim-to-real transfer, where rollouts are costly. Guidance is mixed on weak wrists and harmful on a locked wrist, when the classifier lacks data or favors infeasible motions. Collecting more target-body data with guided $\pi_0$ can fill such gaps: on one weak-wrist arm, guided $\pi_0$ solved a task on which unguided $\pi_0$ had zero successes in the original data, and retraining the classifier on the guided successes raised success from 52.5% to 70.7%.

author: Aaron Wilhelm, Marina de Albuquerque Marcon, Emith Uyanwatte, Nils Napp
title: Micro-Localization: High-Precision Mobile Robot Localization Using Microscopic Ground Texture
content:
arXiv:2610.22563v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We demonstrate high-precision global localization using natural ground texture viewed through microscope optics, achieving localization in the tens-of-micrometers regime. For the planar ground texture localization problem considered here, we relate optical magnification and image-space localization uncertainty to physical localization precision. Leveraging this relationship, we then develop a microscope-based localization system that addresses the calibration, camera-modeling, and focus challenges introduced by high-magnification imaging. We evaluate this system across several surface textures using a calibrated precision gantry. Across 1,007 held-out queries per surface, the system localizes every query and achieves translation RMSEs of 28$-$73 $\mu$m. Independent photometric registration agrees with the feature-based localization estimates to within approximately 9 $\mu$m RMSE. We further demonstrate localization on a low-cost mobile robot using the gantry-collected maps, and also show that the system can resolve micrometer-scale displacement caused by thermal expansion. These results show that microscopic natural surface texture can bring mobile localization into a precision regime typically associated with fixed positioning systems.

author: Victoria Smelova, Daniil Kazachkov, Georgiy Kazantsev, Iuliia Tsvetkova, Egor Cherepanov, Nikita Kac
title: When Plans Change, Remember: Replanning-Guided Visual Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
content:
arXiv:2610.22556v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon, multi-stage Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies often require visual information that is no longer present in the current observation. Retaining the complete observation history is computationally expensive and highly redundant, motivating selective visual memory. We introduce RePlanMem-VLA (Replanning-Guided Keyframe Memory for VLA), which turns a policy's own plan revisions into an online memory-write signal. Under receding-horizon execution, consecutive action chunks predict some of the same future actions. RePlanMem-VLA treats unusually large disagreement between these temporally aligned predictions as evidence of a task-relevant event. We first compare 35 disagreement measures across single-task autoregressive decoder-only and Flow-Matching Transformers trained from scratch, then validate the selected signals on pretrained OpenVLA-OFT and $\pi_{0.5}$ policies over MIKASA-Robo-VLA tasks. The resulting detectors achieve ROC-AUC of 0.981-0.997. We then use the selected signals in RePlanMem-VLA to trigger updates to a bounded visual memory, with a robot-masked write filter suppressing redundant frames. In the evaluated memory-retention experiments, RePlanMem-VLA preserves task-relevant observations until the later decision point in 100% of episodes. Real-robot replay data further show that event selection and redundancy suppression extend beyond simulation. These results establish plan revision as a policy-internal signal for controlling what a VLA remembers. Website: https://vika787.github.io/RePlanMem/.

author: Jan Steckel, Vincent Katter, Wouter Jansen
title: RTISSLAM-3D: Full 6-DoF SLAM With an In-Air 3D Imaging Sonar
content:
arXiv:2610.22552v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Echolocating bats navigate dense forests using sonar alone, and in-air 3D imaging sonars now capture the entire frontal hemisphere with every pulse. Sonar SLAM, however, has so far been planar: current systems estimate a 2D trajectory and discard the elevation information in the sonar images, an assumption that does not hold on rough and sloped terrain such as a forest floor. In this paper, we introduce RTISSLAM-3D, a novel 6-DoF SLAM system for a wheeled robot that carries an in-air 3D imaging sonar, an IMU and wheel encoders. A CFAR detector on the sphere reduces every sonar image to a sparse set of 3D detections, which we use for a 3D acoustic odometry that models the shape of the sonar beam, for place recognition with polar submap descriptors, and for the verification of loop closures by 3D registration, all combined in a 6-DoF pose graph with attitude factors. We evaluated RTISSLAM-3D on a 545m drive through a forest, with a 3D lidar SLAM as reference. The loop closures reduced the horizontal error of the acoustic odometry from 1.74m to 0.28m, with a height error of 0.12m, and 94.6% of the resulting 3D sonar map lies within 0.3 m of the lidar map.

author: Runhan Huang, Xiangcheng Zhang, Haoyu Chen, Yitong Li, Yen-Jen Wang, Bohan Lyu, Haotian Ye, Chuye Ho
title: Scaling Online Exploration for Robot Agents
content:
arXiv:2610.22496v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robot learning has advanced by scaling demonstration datasets and model capacity; however, deploying a new robot embodiment or task typically necessitates a dedicated teleoperation corpus. The resulting policies remain bounded by their imitation distributions, limiting generalization and continual self-improvement. We introduce RAX (Robot Agent eXploration), an open-source framework for robot agents centered on scaling exploration: enabling agents to improve by acquiring online experience and synthesizing executable programs. In RAX, a general-purpose coding agent generates robot control code, operating without action demonstration data, hand-engineered action primitives, or value-function guidance. Through online exploration, the agent identifies decision sequences that achieve task goals and compiles them into modular programs encapsulating the full perception-planning-control loop. Using RAX, we present a systematic multi-embodiment study on scaling online exploration across precision and long-horizon manipulation tasks using single-arm, bimanual, dexterous, mobile, and humanoid systems in simulation and on real robots. Generalization performance on unseen environments improves consistently as exploration scales. In simulation, RAX outperforms top baseline models by +37.4% on average. On real robots, RAX autonomously learns memory-dependent, articulated, high-precision, deformable, and long-horizon mobile manipulation tasks without human demonstrations, continually improving performance by composing verified skills from prior exploration sessions. As exploration scales, we observe emergent capabilities including active perception, error recovery, safety guardrails, and human-robot collaboration. We open-source RAX as a generalist robot-agent platform in which new robot embodiments are integrated through their APIs alone, without teleoperated data collection or policy training.

author: SenseNova, Joint Research Team,  :, Zhongang Cai, Ziang Cao, Tailai Chen, Han Chong Chua, Linjun Da
title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
content:
arXiv:2610.22471v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: GPT-6-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments. In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field. First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT-6-Astra. We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under a unified protocol that allows in-context learning (ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig. 1). Future research may focus on improving 1) the generality of ICL 2) cost and execution time, 3) physical-state verification, 4) recovery from irreversible failures, and 5) long-horizon preservation of progress. Second, we study the agentic harness for embodied control. We identify that close-loop coordination between a high-level "System 2" reasoner (i.e., GPT-6-Astra) and a low-level "System 1" controller (e.g., {\pi}0.5) is costly but effective. Third, we examine GPT-6-Astra on real-world deployment. Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints. Fourth, we envision the next generation of embodied benchmarks. We develop a prototype that 1) derives tasks from real-world needs, 2) provides no in-domain demonstrations, and 3) judges agents on a world clock that keeps running while they deliberate. Taken together, our results suggest that GPT-6-Astra has largely crossed the threshold of embodied competence, but not yet that of practical embodied intelligence.

author: Wei Wang (Robostreet research team. Cambridge, MA, USA), Yiru Veronika Wang (Robostreet research tea
title: Mothership: A Two Tier Autonomous Refuse Collection System for Pedestrian Campuses
content:
arXiv:2610.22461v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Refuse collection in pedestrian campuses, parks and mixed-use districts remains manual because compaction trucks cannot reach bins located on walkways, courtyards and building service doors. This paper presents Mothership, a two-tier autonomous refuse collection system in which an electric compaction truck (the mothership) carries two low-speed sidewalk robots (RoboCarts) that fetch standard two-wheel bins, deliver them to the truck, return the empty bins to their original positions and re-dock on the truck for charging. The architecture separates responsibilities by scale: the truck performs road driving, compaction, lifting and energy supply, while the carts perform only sidewalk transport and bin grasping. This split removes the lift-and-tip mechanism from the sidewalk vehicle, keeping it light and low, and relaxes cart-to-truck docking tolerance to the +/-100 mm capture window of a standard automated lifter. We describe the system architecture, the bin-handling and docking interfaces, and a mission-planning formulation that decomposes a route into truck stop points and cart tasks. A discrete-event simulation over synthetic campus layouts with 2-16 bins/ha quantifies throughput as a function of bin density, cart count and stop-point radius. A two-cart configuration serves 20-29 bins/h. Throughput is governed by an interaction between cart count and stop-point radius: a single cart performs best with many close stops, whereas three or four carts need wide stops (80 m) to stay busy, reaching 35-49 bins/h at moderate-to-high densities. The best stop radius therefore has to be chosen together with the fleet size, not fixed in advance.

author: Wei Wang (Robostreet research team Cambridge, MA, USA), Yiru Veronika Wang (Robostreet research team
title: DriveWorld3D Evidence Constrained 3D World Modeling and Generative Simulation for Real-World Autonomous Driving
content:
arXiv:2610.22450v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Three dimensional modeling for autonomous driving must continuously estimate road geometry, obstacle occupancy, traffic participant behavior, and observational uncertainty under limited computational resources. Existing reconstruction methods can synthesize realistic novel views, but visual fidelity does not sufficiently characterize the geometric reliability required for driving. Generative world models can expand scenarios and predict future observations, yet may introduce content unsupported by measurements. We propose DriveWorld3D, a framework combining temporal video learning, measurement constraints from multiple sensors, and offline generative simulation. Its online component maintains a unified world state comprising road surfaces, volumetric occupancy, dynamic entities, and road relations, while separately representing physical occupancy, observability, and evidence provenance. Action conditioned future prediction and risk sensitive planning connect this representation to driving decisions. Its offline component reconstructs recorded scenes using neural radiance fields or 3D Gaussian Splatting, then expands long tail conditions using generative models while restricting the use of generated content as geometric ground truth. We specify data partitioning, sensor ablations, fault injection, paired closed loop testing, and real to simulation consistency assessment. The central hypothesis is that explicit evidence management can reduce dangerous false free space predictions and occlusion risk within a matched computational budget while retaining acceptable driving efficiency. All performance claims remain subject to experimental validation. Keywords: autonomous driving; 3D occupancy; sensor fusion; uncertainty; generative world models; NeRF; 3D Gaussian Splatting; closed loop simulation

author: Jonathan W. Hurst
title: The Robot I Didn’t Expect to Build
content:
Agility Robotics, the company I cofounded out of my robotics lab at Oregon State University in 2015, has just launched Digit 5. It’s designed to be the first humanoid robot that can safely and economically do useful work at scale, allowing us to bring tens of thousands of humanoid workers into the real world. Engineered to lift 23-kilogram bins onto high shelves and with a battery that can run for 90 minutes on a 9-minute charge, Digit 5’s goal is to handle heavy warehouse tasks shift after shift, filling the need for labor in jobs that are too physically stressful or too dull for humans to want to do.

Digit 5 is what Agility has been working toward for over a decade. But the robot is heavy and bulky, lacking the graceful natural motion of its predecessors, and it’s farther than I thought possible from the robot I dreamed of building when I started this company. To deliver a useful commercial product, Agility has taken a path that is very different from what I first imagined.
From ATRIAS to Digit
My dream has always been to build robots that combine locomotion and manipulation to move through the world and interact with it as people do. I seek a mastery of motion, achieved through devices designed to navigate the constraints of physics with elegance. When I started the Dynamic Robotics Laboratory at Oregon State in 2008, we began with a theory derived from decades of work in biomechanics: that a simple “spring-mass” model (a body supported by legs that act like springs) should be able to reproduce every known walking and running gait found in animals.
We put theory into practice by building the bipedal robot ATRIAS—short for “Assume The Robot Is A Sphere,” a joke among physicists about reducing a complex system to its simplest possible form. author: 36氪
title: 聚焦在轨服务，要打造太空机器人集群，「国宇星辰」完成近亿元A轮融资｜36氪首发
content:
文 | 阿至
商业航天的叙事，正在从“把卫星送上天”过渡至“卫星上天后”怎么管、怎么运营。
除了组网建设加速，一个直观的信号是，低轨星座的补网压力也正在逼近。根据NASA戈达德航天中心此前发布的研究数据，2020至2024年间，有583颗星链卫星从极低地球轨道坠落。而为了防止失控与碰撞，卫星的主动变轨和避让动作也变得愈发频繁。根据SpaceX 7月向美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）提交的报告，仅半年内，星链卫星执行的避让动作次数就超20万次。
当几万颗卫星陆续铺满近地轨道，问题被摆到台前：谁来负责太空中的“管、修、加、清”？
答案在国外已经有人跑通。日本的Astroscale 以碎片清理起家，2024年登陆东京证券交易所，营收四年增长约五倍；意大利的D-Orbit用20余次轨道运输任务验证了客户付费意愿；美国Space Logistics的MEV-1在2020年完成首次商业在轨延寿，为一颗工作了19年的GEO卫星续命五年。根据Fortune Business Insights的报告，全球在轨服务市场正处于稳定增长通道，预计从2026年的31.8亿美元增长至2034年的68.7亿美元，复合年增长率（CAGR）为10.10%。
需求已至，国内卡位者批量涌现。一家低调布局了四年的公司，正在加速其产品的在轨验证。
36氪获悉，国宇星辰（上海）航天科技有限公司（以下简称国宇星辰）已于近期完成近亿元A轮融资，由沂景资本、复星创富、路遥资本联合投资。在此之前，国宇星辰已完成三轮融资，资方包括元禾原点、厚雪资本、尚颀资本等机构。
国宇星辰成立于2022年，创始人张龙拥有超20年航天科研、工程管理与企业管理经验，曾供职于航天科技集团，深度参与国家载人航天、探月及火星探测等重大专项，历任型号主任设计师、集团处长，2015至2021年期间担任蓝箭航天总裁。公司核心技术团队来自中科院微小卫星创新研究院、航天科技集团、清华大学等，具备飞行器研制、发射任务运营和型号工程任务管理能力。
聚焦在轨服务领域，国宇星辰核心业务覆盖在轨服务（辅助入轨/离轨，在轨加注、在轨维修）、在轨组装、太空制造和深空开发。
由国宇星辰自主研发的太空机器人，则是执行上述具体任务的核心载体。
在国宇星辰的定义里，它是一套软硬件一体的空间作业系统，包含躯体、感知、大脑、执行四个部分。
其中，躯体（智能平台和组合动力）实现轨道机动和姿态调整；感知（多源融合AI感知模组）用于对合作目标/非合作目标的精准识别、定位和引导；大脑（星载AI决策单元）能够在通信时延下进行本地任务规划和自主决策；执行（太空灵巧机械臂和加注接口）则需要完成抓取、对接、维修、加注等复杂物理交互。

国宇星辰产品规划
去年5月21日，国宇星辰自研验证星“星迹源一号”在酒泉卫星发射中心成功发射，是国内首个由商业航天公司研制并完成飞行任务的在轨服务及天地感知新技术验证平台，累计在轨时长超一年。
一个进展是，国宇星辰已进入国家级卫星互联网星座运营商的供应商名录。星迹源二号计划于2027年一季度发射，将增加其自研的七自由度机械臂进行在轨验证，这也是国宇星辰核心技术版图中的最后一块拼图。
四年蛰伏，一次反共识的创业
把时间拉回到2022年，中国商业航天赛道已经走过第一轮从过热到退烧的周期，市场趋于冷静，疫情则进一步加剧了创业公司要面对的外部复杂性。当时，行业的主流叙事集中在火箭和卫星，除了“国家队”，在轨服务鲜有商业公司涉足。
一个造火箭出身的老航天人，按照经验和能力惯性，出来创业最容易“找钱”的路可能是继续做运载——先解决进入太空的问题。但张龙的选择恰恰相反，他一头扎进了在轨服务这个在当时看起来有点冷、甚至反共识的赛道。
方向的判断主要来自三个层面。从太空安全和国家战略方向来看，我国大力发展卫星互联网是必然选择，在轨服务从长期来看具备产业基础和用户方向；其次，中国商业航天从2015年起步到2022年前后已经走过一轮发展周期，火箭公司技术迭代和发射验证提速，这意味着进入太空的能力和成本降低进入可预期的阶段；未来随着产业成熟度的提升，下游运营服务拥有更高的附加值和市场空间。
“2015年商业公司开始造火箭的时候，也有很多人不看好，但后来的事实证明：反共识恰恰是早期赛道的机会。”在张龙看来，在轨服务产品有研制周期、验证周期，还有被客户认知的周期，等需求真正爆发再介入就晚了。
还有另外一个更感性版本的答案是，“那个时间点，确实是看到了一束光，我们想追光。”
和张龙一样看好这个方向的还有吴树范和容建刚。作为国宇星辰联合创始人兼首席科学家，吴树范是国际宇航科学院院士、国家引进的海外高层次微小卫星专家，拥有30余年航空航天领域的学术研究、技术开发和产业创新经验，把控公司整体技术方向；CTO容建刚曾供职于中国科学院微小卫星创新研究院，参与过天宫二

author: 36氪
title: 36氪首发丨覆盖半导体产业链多环节，这家国产碳化硅材料企业完成超亿元C轮融资
content:
作者 | 乔钰杰
编辑 | 袁斯来
本文约1500字，建议阅读4分钟
硬氪获悉，浙江六方半导体有限公司（以下简称“六方半导体”）近日完成超亿元C1轮股权融资，本轮由北京仓廪资本与诸暨产业投资集团有限公司联合出资。
六方半导体成立于2018年，专注于半导体新材料的研发与生产，业务覆盖半导体长晶、外延、刻蚀等关键工艺环节，为下游客户提供核心材料及精密零部件解决方案。
公司掌握CVD‑SiC碳化硅材料合成核心技术，依托该技术推出导流桶、单晶硅外延托盘、LED芯片外延托盘、SiC聚焦环等产品，覆盖半导体产业链多个环节。
在碳化硅长晶原料制备方面，六方半导体采用气相法制备高纯碳化硅粉料，具备高纯度、高密度、低氮含量等特性。目前公司产品性能可对标海外同类产品，已逐步导入国内主流长晶厂商。同时，基于CVD-SiC核心技术，公司不断拓展高纯SiC材料的应用领域，包括高纯SiC原料及薄膜在光学，芯片散热，异构集成等领域的应用。
六方半导体成立之初聚焦碳化硅涂层芯片外延托盘的国产替代。经过持续研发，公司掌握了CVD-SiC涂层的量产设备及工艺的核心技术，实现了碳化硅涂层芯片外延托盘的国产替代。
在此基础上，公司进一步突破整体SiC生长制备及加工技术。整体SiC材料是半导体领域众多核心零部件基础材料，包括刻蚀工艺所需要聚焦环，RTP设备所需的边缘环等。

（图源/企业）
随着3D NAND向300层以上推进，刻蚀工艺所需步骤数从50步向100步以上增加。AI算力芯片扩产则进一步拉动了刻蚀设备装机数量，作为刻蚀设备的核心耗材，CVD-SiC刻蚀环的需求量随之大增。目前国内CVD-SiC聚焦环国产化率不足15%，7nm以下的先进制程所需的聚焦环国产化率不足5%。
六方半导体创始人何少龙博士牵头承担了“大尺寸超高纯碳化硅制备关键技术”国家重点研发计划，针对CVD-SiC快速沉积的科学问题以及高硬脆材料的高效加工技术难题展开科学攻关，最终实现国产替代和产业化。
公司创始人何少龙博士毕业于浙江大学物理系，曾先后在日本广岛大学、国立材料研究所开展研究，回国后任职于中科院物理所、宁波材料所，从事凝聚态物理研究，已在《Nature Materials》《Nature Communications》《Phys. Rev. Lett.》《PNAS》等国际期刊发表30余篇学术论文，多次受邀在美国March Meeting、日本半导体年会、香山会议等国内外顶级学术会议做特邀报告；现任国家重点研发计划首席科学家、浙江省级领军人才。
公司本轮融资资金将重点用于前沿新品研发及产能扩建，占地100亩的新厂房预计2026年12月正式投产。

（图源/企业）
以下为创始人问答：
硬氪：接下来公司的前沿产品研发主要会投向哪些方向？
何少龙：目前我们已经在拓展的方向，包括碳化硅材料在光学及芯片散热领域的应用。
碳化硅具有较高的折射率，在AR眼镜以及Meta lens等领域均有很高的应用价值。我们希望拓展碳化硅薄膜沉积技术，进一步延伸到光学领域的应用。
另一方面，碳化硅的热导率理论值最高可以到500W/(m·K)，是非常理想的散热材料，我们将拓展SiC材料在芯片散热领域的应用。
投资方观点
仓廪资本：半导体核心材料与关键工艺零部件是国内半导体产业链实现自主可控的核心基石，也是硬科技领域长期具备高成长价值的黄金赛道。六方半导体团队多年来在材料领域的深度技术积累和扎实的产业化落地能力，具备突出的行业稀缺性。未来投资方将充分调动自身的产业资源网络，在客户对接、技术协同等方面为企业提供全方位赋能，助力企业快速成长为赛道内的核心领军企业。
诸暨产投：本次投资是地方国有产业投资平台围绕半导体先进材料赛道的关键战略布局。后续将充分依托诸暨本地的产业配套优势与政策支持体系，为六方半导体新厂区落地建设、区域产业链生态对接提供全流程保障，推动企业在诸暨扎根发展，共同带动区域半导体新材料产业集群的成型与壮大。

 从八千平米到两千八
本月底，优衣库上海全球旗舰店将在淮海中路755号重新开门。几百米外的淮海中路887号，开了13年的旧店也随之谢幕。
淮海中路887号的优衣库上海全球旗舰店于2013年开业，至今仍是优衣库全球最大的门店，从地下一层延伸到地上五层，营业面积超过8000平方米，即将搬迁的新址面积约2800平方米，不到原址的一半。
开业前夕，柳井正曾亲赴上海并接受媒体采访，“3000家门店”的目标也是那个时候提出的。开业当日，迅销高层悉数到场剪彩，中国区CEO潘宁称，这标志着优衣库在中国进入了“新的发展阶段”。
这次搬迁宣布一个多月后，迅销公布了2026财年财报：优衣库北美和欧洲的合计收入约8775亿日元，首次超大中华区；占集团收入的比重也分别达到22.1%和18.3%，欧美同样首次反超大中华区。

在淮海中路全球旗舰店强劲势头的带动下，优衣库母公司迅销集团2013财年的全球总销售额首度突破1兆日圆
过去很长一段时间里，大中华区都是优衣库在日本之外最重要的“现金牛”：2021财年，它贡献了迅销集团四分之一的收入，优衣库海外业务约九成的经营利润也来自这里。五年前，大中华区撑起了优衣库海外收入的57%，如今这一比重已降至30%。五年里，优衣库在欧美的收入扩大到约3.6倍，包括港台在内的大中华区只增长了约三分之一。
欧美市场的快速增长，也让迅销在年销售额上首次超过H&M，跃升为全球第二大服装零售商，仅次于Zara母公司Inditex。
在萎靡一年多之后，大中华区在2026财年重回增长，收入同比增长11.3%，但若以人民币计，中国大陆市场的增幅只有3%，曾经的引擎角色很难再回来。未来十年，欧美市场不但可以接棒，柳井正还公开表示，“澳洲、印度和东南亚市场的渗透率还有大幅提升的空间。”
疫情之后，优衣库一度宣布在中国每年新开“80到100家”门店，并向低线城市下沉。中国大陆门店数量在2024财年末达到926家的峰值。
这一策略的效果并不算好，因为低线市场的折扣和平替现象更为严重。2025财年，优衣库大中华区收入下滑4%，业务利润下滑12.5%，这是疫情之后的首次下滑。随后，优衣库开始收缩门店，提出“关小店，开大店”，并淡化3000家店的目标以及每年新开店数量。有零售人士指出，面积大小并非真正的标准，优衣库此举实际上是在关闭效率不佳的店铺，低线城市则以电商先行。
柳井正没有在最新的财报季公开谈论中国，最近一次表态要追溯到2025年。那时，他批评中国门店“总部一声令下、全国统一行动”的做法，认为必须要将粗放转为单店自主经营。
在他看来，中国员工和经营者的素质很高，正是借助连锁经营的优势，才把业务做到了今天的规模，“但现状是，门店按照总部指令整齐划一行动的倾向很强，没能做出适合各地顾客的商品组合和卖场”。要打破这一局面，“各门店必须自己动脑、自己做生意，向个店经营转型”。

制图：36氪
有零售分析人士向36氪指出，对于线下零售品牌来说，靠多开店抢渠道的时代已经过去了。“开店仍然有用，只是从主要的增长手段，变成了辅助手段。”
他给出了两个原因。一是新开的商场越来越少，同一个商圈里店开多了，就会互相抢客人，一家新店能带来的增量越来越小，甚至得不偿失。二是电商、直播和私域分走了越来越多的生意，线下门店的用途也变了：不再只是卖货的地方，更多是让顾客来试穿、了解品牌，或者充当就近发货的仓库。
2026财年，优衣库在中国大陆净关店51家，门店数量降至851家。大幅关店之后，按日元计，大中华区单店年营收终于超过了2019年的水平。优衣库从未公开大中华区的营业面积，但假设它正如其所说，关掉的是小店、开的是大店，单位面积收入恐不及疫情前。
种种迹象表明，优衣库正在依靠中国以外的海外市场，实现柳井正反复重申的“年收入十万亿日元”的宏大目标。
下一篇章
“判断进入市场的时机是否成熟，通常有三个要点：消费者是否欢迎我们，宏观和微观环境是否最为适合，以及我们是否做好了服务新市场的准备。”2019年，一位优衣库负责海外市场的高管这样告诉媒体。
如今，这一时机已经到来——全球地缘冲突不断之下导致供应链中断，能源价格飙升，欧美国家通膨反弹，民众继续削减可选消费，服饰也是其中之一。
有行业人士向36氪表示，欧美市场长期缺乏“中等价位、具有实穿性和设计感，不过分追求潮流”的���牌，优衣库很好地填补了这个空白。即使面对关税等影响小幅提价之后，优衣库仍然很有价格优势。
笔者实地探访柏林市中心的优衣库门店发现，秋冬款的定价大约是国内的1.2到1.5倍，部分主力单品，例如薄款羽绒服和饺子包，定价与国内基本持平。而按汇率折算，柏林人均可支配收入约为上海的2.4倍，优衣库在当地的价格竞争力十足。

author: 36氪
title: 飞利浦把剃须刀做成随身配饰，年轻化能否打开新市场？｜最前线
content:
36氪获悉，10月16日，飞利浦在上海发布第三代便携式剃须刀「萤火虫」。与传统电动剃须刀强调剃净效率、刀头技术和续航能力不同，这款产品采用小巧机身、六种配色、磁吸开合与呼吸灯设计，试图将日常理容与年轻人的穿搭、出行和社交场景联系起来。
这背后是飞利浦对男士理容消费人群的一次细分。相较于面向成熟消费者的传统剃须刀，飞利浦希望通过设计、便携性和相对亲民的价格，吸引更年轻的用户，并让电动剃须刀成为他们的第一把剃须刀。
飞利浦大中华区高级副总裁、健康生活事业群总经理吴品慧在媒体群访中表示，中国剃须刀市场已经相对成熟，但仍有不少消费者使用手动剃须刀。飞利浦希望借助新品降低消费者尝试电动剃须刀的门槛，将其从一件功能性工具变成兼顾理容、护肤与个性表达的消费品。

飞利浦第三代便携式剃须刀「萤火虫」
这一思路并非单纯依靠外观变化。飞利浦大中华区健康生活事业群男士理容事业部总经理冯雪表示，品牌从三四年前便开始围绕年轻消费者开展调研，并跟随消费者出游、运动，观察产品在实际生活中的使用方式。团队发现，29岁以下的消费者既希望快速完成剃须，也在意产品外观和使用体验，希望日常用品能够体现个人风格。
萤火虫的设计由此呈现出一些不同于传统剃须刀的特征。产品重119克，采用磁吸上盖和带有灯光反馈的按键设计，通过不同灯光对应剃须模式；功能方面则搭载3D浮动刀头，并提供敏感肌模式。按照飞利浦公布的信息，产品支持3分钟快充，续航最长可达40天。公司试图将便携、快速剃须与视觉设计结合，让产品能够出现在通勤、健身、露营等浴室之外的场景。
不过，把剃须刀做得更像潮流单品，并不意味着功能竞争已经退居次要位置。对剃须产品而言，剃净效果、皮肤刺激、使用便利性和耐用程度仍然是决定复购的重要因素。灯光和配色可以带来初次购买的新鲜感，但能否形成持续需求，仍取决于产品在日常使用中的表现。飞利浦在采访中强调，萤火虫并未因体积缩小而牺牲性能，但相关性能优势仍需要通过实际使用和消费者反馈来检验。
从产品矩阵来看，萤火虫也不是飞利浦便携剃须刀业务的孤立尝试。2024年，飞利浦推出鹅卵石系列，主要面向中高端消费及礼赠需求；此次萤火虫进一步向年轻人延伸。与此同时，飞利浦还在高端产品线上推进带有屏幕定制、智能感应等功能的新品，尝试覆盖不同消费能力与理容需求的人群。
这意味着，飞利浦的策略并不是让所有消费者购买同一种剃须刀，而是通过价格、功能和设计的差异建立更细致的产品梯队。对于一个已经拥有成熟产品与品牌认知的企业而言，推出面向年轻人的产品，可以在不完全改变核心技术路线的情况下，拓展新的消费场景。
价格则是这套策略能否成立的另一关键。吴品慧表示，品牌希望通过相对亲民的定价，让电动剃须刀成为更多年轻男性的入门选择。不过，对于年轻消费者而言，外观和情绪价值固然能够影响购买决策，但如果产品价格超出其日常用品的预算，场景化设计未必足以支撑购买。
飞利浦同时希望将中国市场打造为全球创新的重要来源。吴品慧表示，品牌过去几年持续在中国推进本土研发和产品创新，并希望将中国消费者认可的产品与营销经验带向其他市场。萤火虫所体现的本土化方向，是将年轻消费者的审美偏好和生活方式纳入产品设计，而不只是将海外成熟产品引入中国销售。
从行业经营的角度看，这种尝试能否产生实际增量，最终仍需要回到销售表现、用户结构和复购情况。年轻化设计可以让一件成熟品类重新获得关注，却不必然意味着消费者愿意为此增加预算。对于飞利浦而言，萤火虫真正需要验证的，不只是年轻人是否喜欢一把会发光、可以随身携带的剃须刀，而是这种设计能否转化为稳定的购买需求，并为成熟的电动剃须刀市场带来新的消费者。

author: IT之家
title: 商务部：今年 1-9 月，重点平台智能眼镜销售额增长 1.1 倍
content:
IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，国新办今日举行新闻发布会，介绍加快推进科技兴商有关情况。
商务部部长助理袁晓明介绍，本次《关于加快推进科技兴商的意见》（IT之家注：以下简称《意见》）是立足新发展阶段，首次以“科技兴商”为主题，出台的一份综合性、系统性文件。核心是把科技创新作为贯穿商贸全链条的重要驱动力，推动科技与商贸深度融合。政策的主要特点，可以用三个字来概括：“新”“全”“实”。
“新”，就是突出科技创新，适应消费新趋势新变化。随着人民生活水平提升，消费者更加注重产品的品质和消费体验。根据商务部商务大数据显示，今年 1-9 月，重点平台智能眼镜销售额增长 1.1 倍。人工智能、物联网、区块链等新技术，在消费领域广泛应用，科技创新日益成为推动消费扩容升级的重要举措。《意见》紧扣新一轮科技革命和产业变革，既立足当前扩大消费的现实需要，着力激活消费市场；又着眼长远发展，以科技创新改造提升传统商贸、培育壮大新兴业态，为商贸高质量发展注入持久动力。
“全”，就是突出双向发力，覆盖商贸全链条全业态。纵向上，从供给端的产品研发、生产制造、服务提供，到流通端的批发、物流、电商，再到消费场景，将科技创新融入到商贸各环节。横向上，既用新技术改造提升零售、餐饮、家政等传统业态，让传统的消费焕发新活力；同时，也培育商业智能体、绿色循环消费等新业态新模式，让新型消费释放新动能，形成供需两端协同、传统消费与新型消费并举的完整政策体系。
“实”，就是突出问题导向，确保政策可落地可检验。《意见》聚焦商贸领域突出问题精准施策。例如，针对商品供需适配问题，提出发展柔性制造、推广按需生产等模式，培育一批具有行业影响力的定制品牌。围绕丰富优质服务供给，提出推动家政、医疗、养老托育等民生服务数智化转型，拓展智慧教育、智慧文旅、智能体育等升级服务。针对电商品质问题，提出开展品质电商培育行动，加强重点产品电商平台联网核查。

author: IT之家
title: 英特尔 CEO 陈立武称中国芯片制造“目前并未落后太多”
content:
IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，英特尔 CEO 陈立武近日接受《日经亚洲》采访时表示，在芯片制造技术方面，中国与美国的差距并不大。

中美芯片制造技术领域的差距，一直是科技业界的热门话题。埃隆 · 马斯克（IT之家注：Elon Musk）曾认为，中国最快只需要两到三年就能突破现有限制。而蔡司半导体业务负责人认为，在最新的 EUV 技术方面，中国落后 15 年是比较合理的预计。

author: IT之家
title: 2026 年三季度印度智能手机市场遇冷，iPhone 销量下滑 20%
content:
IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，市场调研机构 Omdia 数据显示，2026 年第三季度，印度全国智能手机出货量同比下降 26%，创下过去 10 年同期最低水平。尽管苹果 iPhone 在印度的销量同比下滑 20%，但与竞争对手相比，其表现仍相对稳健。

据悉，印度消费者的消费支出趋于保守，与新机涨价叠加在一起，该国智能手机总出货量降至 3580 万部。零售商也采取了更为谨慎的策略，在购物季到来前避免囤积过多库存。
尽管销量下滑 20%，苹果仍以 390 万部的出货量位列印度智能手机市场第五，iPhone 16 和 iPhone 17 等标准版机型占大头。由于苹果今年没有推出 iPhone 18 标准版，因此不少消费者选择旧款产品。
如今，手机厂商已不能再单纯依靠庞大的出货量推动印度业务增长，而是需要付出更多努力来说服消费者更换手机。在持续低迷的市场环境下，提供更有吸引力的以旧换新优惠、并突出高端调性的品牌，才更有可能站稳脚跟。

author: IT之家
title: 四个谷歌 Gemini 4 Argon 智能体成功击败末影龙通关《我的世界》，耗时 27 小时
content:
IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，谷歌研究人员近日发布论文称，他们使用四个 Gemini 4 Argon 智能体成功通关《我的世界》，仅用 27 小时就成功击败末影龙。

谷歌将 4 个 Gemini 4 放入随机生成的世界中，他们可以通过游戏内的聊天框互相协调。但研究人员没有为他们制定任何策略，只是说了最终目标，所有行为都由智能体自行规划。研究人员可通过仪表板观察他们，下达暂停 / 终止测试指令，但没有权利介入。
游戏开始后，这些智能体很快分担了不同任务：有的建造末影人农场；有的收集食物；有的专注于探索。它们会分享战斗技巧，并在队友死亡后寻回丢失的装备。

整个游戏过程中，4 个智能体发送了 229 条消息、运行 2783 个程序，死亡 605 次。它们花了 13.5 小时才抵达末地，剩下的时间全部用来击败末影龙。整个过程用了 13.5 亿个输入 Token，按照普通用户标准来算，成本约为 1,620 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 10,842 元人民币）。
研究团队表示：“据我们所知，这是 AI 智能体首次在完全自主的情况下从头到尾通关《我的世界》。整个过程仅使用标准的 Mineflayer 库，没有使用种子地图，也没有人类辅助。”
